dep.fix.brewMissing: Homebrew is not installed: install it from brew.sh (the installer asks for your password), then press Check again.
dep.fix.brewOwner: Homebrew's folder belongs to another user, so nothing can be installed: run sudo chown -R $(whoami) /opt/homebrew in Terminal, then install again.
dep.fix.diskspace: The disk is full: free some space (the SDK and toolchains unpack to several GB) and press Install again.
dep.fix.log: The full output is in the log under the Mac/iPhone choice.
dep.fix.metalPin: This is not the Metal compiler the shaders were tested with. Games that use NVN stop before the shader steps. Install Xcode 27.2 (macOS 26.6 or later) and its Metal toolchain.
dep.fix.network: The download failed: check the network (a proxy or VPN can block Homebrew's hosts) and try again.
dep.fix.nonascii: The SDK path contains non-ASCII characters (a Chinese username, for example): ld64.lld on Windows may fail to open it. Copy the whole SDK folder to an ASCII-only path (e.g. C:\NSPB\sdk) and point the dependencies panel's Choose folder… at it.
dep.fix.xcodeLicense: Xcode's license is not accepted yet: run sudo xcodebuild -license accept.
dep.git.downloading: Downloading PortableGit (the SDK download needs it, about 45 MB)…
dep.glslang.hint: compiles OpenGL games' shaders, and the NSP script's environment check requires it
dep.guide.iossdk: Three ways to get it: ① press Install and this app downloads one via mirror (no Apple ID, about 55 MB); ② download iPhoneOS27.2.sdk.zip from iOS-SDKs releases (or Xcode.xip from Apple developer downloads), then press Choose zip / folder… and pick the archive or the unpacked iPhoneOS*.sdk folder; ③ copy the same-named folder from Xcode.app's Platforms/iPhoneOS.platform/Developer/SDKs/ on a Mac that has Xcode.
dep.guide.metal: The Metal shader compiler ships separately from Apple: download "Metal Developer Tools for Windows" from the Apple developer downloads (Apple ID required), then press Choose zip / folder… and pick the downloaded zip, the unpacked folder, or bin\metal.exe inside it. An installed copy is found by itself in the usual places.

dev.copySkipped: Installed on %@, but the game files were not transferred
dev.expiryUnknown: Signature expiry: unknown (re-signing is still offered)
dev.installedNote: The game is on the device, ready to open.
dev.noDevices: No iPhone or iPad paired with this Mac (needs Xcode).
dev.noTeam: No Apple ID in Xcode and no development certificate. Open Xcode → Settings → Apple Accounts (Xcode menus are English-only), sign in with your Apple ID, select Personal Team → Download Manual Profiles. The certificate does not appear immediately — wait ~30 seconds and press Check again. If it still does not appear, click + in Manage Certificates to create an Apple Development certificate manually.
dev.note: Xcode signs the shared app for this device and installs it there, then copies the game data (romfs.img) into the app’s Documents. The first copy of a large game takes a few minutes. The first time, turn on Developer Mode on the device and trust the developer (Settings → General → VPN & Device Management).
dev.reinstallFailed: Reinstalling failed: %@ (if the signature has expired, sign and install again)
dev.reinstallMissing: The signed app is not there: %@ (build again)
dev.reinstalled: Reinstalled on %@ (the game data is kept)
dev.resignFailed: Re-signing failed: %@ (check the certificate in Xcode → Settings → Accounts → Manage Certificates, or the network)
dev.resignHelp: Sign and install again from the cached project: no rebuild, and the app's data (saves, game data) is kept
dev.resignNoProject: The cached Xcode project is not there: %@ (build once more)
dev.resignNoTeam: Re-signing needs a signing team: pick one first.
dev.resignOlder: This game was built as its own app, before there was one shared app. Build it again to put it in the shared app.
dev.saveFailed: Saving the IPA failed: %@ (check free space and write permission at the destination)
dev.saveNeedsApp: No signed app to pack: %@ (build again)
dev.teamNoCert: This team has no development certificate yet: Xcode creates it at the first install (the Mac needs to be online).

engine.autoNote: Installs a newer engine of the selected channel when the app opens
engine.chainChanged: Engine %@ is installed. The shader chain changed from %@ to %@, so every game compiles its shaders again on its next build.
engine.channelNote: Stable is the engine tested with this app version. Experimental follows the newest upstream and is published once it passes the automated checks.
engine.fail.digest: The downloaded engine does not match its checksum. Nothing was installed.
engine.fail.download: The engine could not be downloaded. Check the connection and try again.
engine.fail.install: The engine could not be installed. Check the free space and try again.
engine.fail.manifest: The engine list could not be read. Nothing was installed.
engine.fail.network: Could not reach GitHub to check the engine. Check the connection and try again.
engine.fail.noManifest: The %@ channel has no engine for this app version yet
engine.fail.unsigned: The engine list is not signed with the app's key. Nothing was installed.
engine.seedFail: Could not copy the engine from the app into Application Support. Check the free space and open the app again.
engine.switch.title: Switch the engine channel?
engine.switch.toExperimental: Experimental follows the newest upstream. It passed the automated checks, but nobody has played it yet. If its shader chain differs, every game compiles its shaders again on its next build. Switching back to Stable does the same.
engine.switch.toStable: Stable is the engine tested with this app version. If its shader chain differs from the experimental one, every game compiles its shaders again on its next build.
engine.syncing: Fetching the engine from GitHub (about 80 MB). This runs on the first start and after updates and takes a minute or two.
engine.title: Build engine
engine.upToDate: The engine is up to date (%@)
engine.waitForBuild: A build is running. Try again when it has finished.
engine.waitsForBuild: Engine %@ is installed. The build tools switch to it when the running build has finished.
fail.a32Program.next: Pick the update the profile lists.
fail.a32Program.what: This version is 32-bit and can't run on Apple silicon.
fail.a32Program.whatNamed: This version of %@ is 32-bit and can't run on Apple silicon.
fail.cloudFolder.next: Cloud folders add hidden data to every file. The signing step at the end of the build refuses it. Move your game files out of iCloud Drive, or choose a folder outside it under Save to. Then build again.
fail.cloudFolder.what: The build folder is in iCloud Drive or another cloud folder.
fail.cltSelected.next: Select Xcode with the button below (it asks for an administrator password), or run sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app in Terminal, then build again.
fail.cltSelected.what: The Command Line Tools are selected instead of Xcode, and they have no iOS SDK.
fail.confirm.title: Build anyway?
fail.damagedNSP.next: Dump or download the file again. Building anyway writes the damaged files as they are, which may break the game.
fail.damagedNSP.risk: This writes the damaged files as they are. The game may crash or show wrong data, and the result is untested. The choice applies to this one build and is not saved.
fail.damagedNSP.what: The game file is damaged. It fails the hash check, often from an incomplete copy or a broken download.
fail.devicePairing.next: Connect the device with a cable, tap Trust on the device and enter its passcode. Then try again.
fail.devicePairing.what: This Mac is not paired with the device.
fail.deviceTransfer.next: Unlock the iPhone or iPad and tap Trust if it asks, check the cable and that the device stays connected, then try again.
fail.deviceTransfer.what: Sending the game to the device failed.
fail.diskFull.next: Free up space on the drive that holds the build folder, the one ending in _build beside your game files. Free space in a game's menu removes what a finished build no longer needs. Then build again.
fail.diskFull.what: The drive ran out of free space for the build.
fail.diskFull.whatNeeds: There is not enough free space. The build needs at least %@ GB on the drive.
fail.driveMissing.next: Connect the drive and wait until it shows up in the Finder, then build again.
fail.driveMissing.what: The drive with your game files is not connected.
fail.driveMissing.whatNamed: The drive “%@” with your game files is not connected.
fail.engineOffline.next: Check your internet connection and that github.com can be reached, then press Try again. Games cannot be built without the engine.
fail.engineOffline.what: The engine could not be downloaded from GitHub.
fail.engineSync.next: Press Try again. The log shows the reason. If it keeps failing, report it with Copy diagnostics and the log.
fail.engineSync.what: The engine could not be prepared.
fail.iosSDK.next: Open Xcode → Settings → Components and install iOS, or press the button to run xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS.
fail.iosSDK.what: The iOS SDK is not installed. An iPhone build needs it.
fail.keys.next: Choose your prod.keys again. If it is on an external drive, connect the drive first. Then build again.
fail.keys.what: The keys file was not found or can't be read.
fail.keysOld.next: The game needs a key that came with a newer Switch system version. Update your own Switch, take prod.keys from it again, choose the new file and build again. The log names the key and the system version.
fail.keysOld.what: Your prod.keys file is older than the game.
fail.noSigningAccount.next: Open Xcode > Settings > Accounts, sign in with your Apple ID and make sure the team is listed, then build again. A free Apple ID is enough and Xcode creates the certificate itself.
fail.noSigningAccount.what: Xcode has no signing account for the chosen team.
fail.noTitleID.next:
Rename the file to include its title ID, like Game Name [0100XXXXXXXXXXXX].nsp, using the ID of that exact package, since the base game, an update and DLC each have their own. Then build again.
It can also be that the folder has no .nsp, .xci, .nsz or .xcz files (split or archived parts such as .00 or .rar are not read), or that the files are still in iCloud and not downloaded. Choose Show folder to check.
fail.noTitleID.what: No package in the folder has a title ID the build can read: none has a ticket inside and none has [title ID] in its file name.
fail.otherMetal.next: This game uses NVN and needs Xcode 27.2 (macOS 26.6 or later). Install it and its Metal toolchain, then build again.
fail.otherMetal.risk: This builds with a Metal compiler nobody tested the shaders with. The pictures can come out wrong, the result is untested and it is not supported. The choice applies to this one build and is not saved.
fail.otherMetal.what: This Mac's Metal compiler is not the one the shaders were tested with.
fail.override.note: Build anyway: this build adds %@ (confirmed, not saved)
fail.psoDiskFull.next: Free up space on the drive that holds the build folder, or choose a build folder on another drive. Then build again.
fail.psoDiskFull.what: There is not enough free space to build the Metal shader archive.
fail.psoDiskFull.whatNeeds: The Metal shader archive needs about %@ GB of free space on the build drive.
fail.rosetta.next: NS Port Builder uses its bundled Python when it has one. If this build used another, remove the Intel venv in ~/Library/Application Support/NS Port Builder/venv and press Check again.
fail.rosetta.what: The build script ran with an Intel Python under Rosetta, so the tools it starts would run as Intel code too.
fail.severalGames.choose: Choose the title ID you want to build.
fail.severalGames.next: A build takes one game per folder. Move the other games out of the folder or put this game's files in a folder of their own, then build again.
fail.severalGames.what: The folder holds more than one game.
fail.shaderRegression.next: Please report it with the list in the build log. Building anyway leaves those shaders out, so parts of the picture may be missing.
fail.shaderRegression.risk: This packs the app without those shaders. Parts of the picture may be missing and the result is untested. The choice applies to this one build and is not saved.
fail.shaderRegression.what: Some shaders that translated before fail to translate with this version.
fail.shellDataIncomplete.next: The game is not ready to play. Unlock the device and keep it connected, then retry. Only the missing or incomplete files are copied.
fail.shellDataIncomplete.what: The game data on the device is incomplete.
fail.teamTaken.next: Xcode refused it for your team, also with your team's own variant of the ID. Open Xcode > Settings > Accounts and sign in with the Apple ID that installed this game before, or choose a different signing team here. Then build again.
fail.teamTaken.what: The game's app ID is registered to another Apple team.
fail.translator.next: Reinstall .NET with the button below, then build again. If DOTNET_ROOT names another runtime, unset it.
fail.translator.what: The shader translator does not run. It needs the .NET 10 runtime for this Mac's architecture.
fail.volumeFormat.next: The disk is not formatted as APFS (for example Mac OS Extended). A build can't put a new app over an old one there, so only the first build into a folder works. Choose a folder on an APFS disk under Save to, or move the old .app to the Trash first. Then build again.
fail.volumeFormat.what: This disk can't replace the old Mac app.
fail.zbic.next: Install zbic with the button below, then build again. Or run python3 -m pip install zbic in a terminal, with the Python the build uses.
fail.zbic.what: This game's modules use Nintendo's zstd variant (system 22.0.0 and later), and reading them needs the Python package zbic, which is not installed.
folder.base: Game folder, title ID %@ from main.npdm
folder.engineOld: This engine does not build game folders. Update the engine first.
folder.engineOldNUP: This engine does not build NUP files. Update the engine first.
folder.keys: Not needed. A game folder or a NUP file is not encrypted.
folder.noProfile: The engine has no profile for %@. A game folder builds only a game the engine knows.
folder.nupBaseNoID: NUP file. The build reads its title ID.
folder.problem.dlcName: dlc/%@ is not named with a title ID.
folder.problem.dlcRomFS: dlc/%1$@ needs one romfs folder and has %2$d.
folder.problem.noBase: Put exefs and romfs into a folder named base, then choose this folder again.
folder.problem.notBase: main.npdm names %@, which is not a base game.
folder.problem.notDLC: dlc/%@ is not add-on content of this game.
folder.problem.notNUP: %@ is not a NUP file of format version 1.
folder.problem.npdm: base/exefs/main.npdm cannot be read as an NPDM file.
folder.problem.nupPartial: %@ is not the size its header says. It was probably copied or downloaded only in part.
folder.problem.package: %@ is next to the game's folders. Keep the packages or the folders, not both.
folder.problem.severalNUPs: This folder holds %d NUP files. Keep one game per folder, or choose the NUP file itself.
free.clones: A Mac app built on the same drive shares its game files and shaders with this folder (APFS clones), so removing them can free less than shown.
free.confirmNote: The files are deleted, not moved to the Trash.
free.cost.caches: Build tools, rewritten game code, DLC images and temporary files: the next build makes them again.
free.cost.extracted: The next build extracts the game again.
free.cost.oldShaders: Libraries that earlier versions of the shader chain left. The current build does not use them, so the next build costs nothing. Included in Shader output.
free.cost.shaders: The next build compiles the shaders again, which can take a long time.
free.cost.xcode: The next build prepares and compiles the app again.
free.empty: There is nothing to remove in this game’s build folder.
free.failed: Some files could not be removed: %@
free.keptNote: Logs, the game’s profile, converted NSPs and saves
free.note: Removes this game’s build files, which the next build makes again. The app, the IPA, the game data archive and the NSPs stay.
